chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr, from a mawlā of Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
As for the two rakʿahs of al-watr, if you wish, you may speak between them and the third; and if you wish, you may refrain from doing so.

key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the odd-numbered concluding prayer unit in the night prayer context
key_terms.لَمْ تَفْعَلْ: you do not do so; you refrain from speaking

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak between the two rakʿahs of al-shafʿ and the third rakʿah of al-watr?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the prayer arrangement between the two rakʿahs preceding the final rakʿah of al-watr and the third rakʿah itself. It indicates permissibility regarding speaking between them, showing that speech in that interval is optional and not required to be avoided.
